sections.h2: Selling routes for a Baytown homeowner in a hurry
sections.html:
Baytown sellers can pick an agent, go solo, or sell to a cash buyer who will take the house in any condition. Cash tends to suit owners with a repair backlog, an inherited property, a tenant they want gone, or a lender or court deadline.

About 86,561 people lived in Baytown in mid-2025, and 52.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The middle home value is $197,300, so big repairs can take a large bite out of a listing price.

  • Hiring an agent: right for a sound house if you can allow for open houses and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Selling it yourself: pricing, the contract and buyer questions are yours to handle before a title company closes it.
  • Cash buyer: skips the lender and the repair demands, then sets a closing date after one quick walk-through.

The midpoint rent is $1,307. Owners spend $1,761 monthly with a loan and $691 without. Population has crept up only 1.2 percent over the 2020 baseline of 85,547, following the rise from 71,802 residents in 2010.

The middle household income is $59,910 in 2024 dollars, and the average commute takes 25.4 minutes. Parts of the city began as company housing in the 1920s, when the refinery operator financed employee homes. Anyone buying an older Baytown house will therefore ask about age, plumbing and foundation.

It varies by parcel. Baytown lies in southeastern Harris County and stretches east into Chambers County, which means two sets of county offices cover the city.

That split settles who files your deed, who values the lot and who mails the bill. Search the wrong county and the parcel will not come up.

  • Your tax bill lists the county and account number at the top.
  • Ask the closing agent to name the clerk who will record the deed.
  • On a lot near the county line, review the school and other districts printed on the bill.

On the Comptroller's property tax basics page, you will see that values are fixed as of January 1 and bills are sent around October 1.

sections.h2: Nightly rentals and what a buyer can count on
sections.html:
Under Baytown's land development code, a nightly rental in a residential or mixed-use district needs a Special Use Permit approved by City Council. The first request was approved with conditions for an existing house in a Suburban Residential district.

Staff later drafted an amendment to swap that vote for a standard permit process in those districts. Council also weighed annual permits and inspections, along with occupancy and parking limits, so the rules may have changed by the time you list.

Has your house hosted paying guests? Planning staff can tell you which rule covers the address and whether an approval is on record. A buyer who is counting on rental income should confirm the status with the city before signing. The city's amendment notice describes the proposal.

sections.h2: Selling a house you inherited in Baytown
sections.html:
The title papers you need depend on how the house came to you. Four years after the death is the normal limit for probating a will, and a court can allow a later filing for good reason. Heirs usually choose among four routes.

  • Muniment of title: works when the estate's only debts are liens on real estate. File the court order and the will with the clerk where the land sits.
  • Small estate affidavit: limited to $75,000 in assets beyond the homestead. It rarely fits real property, with the exception of a homestead going to a spouse or minor children.
  • Affidavit of heirship: a sworn statement and nothing more; a title company is under no legal duty to take it.
  • Executor's or administrator's deed: signed once a court has appointed the person.

An heir left off the recorded deed can keep a homestead exemption by handing the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill. The State Law Library's informal probate guide explains each route, and a probate lawyer can tell you which one fits your estate.

sections.h2: Back taxes when a Baytown house sells
sections.html:
Taxes follow the house. Each year's lien takes hold on January 1, so any unpaid tax is deducted from your proceeds at closing. Bills come in October. Once February 1 arrives, an unpaid account is delinquent and adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

Behind on a homestead? Some collectors offer payment plans of up to 36 months, so ask. Waivers of penalty and interest are narrow: you must pay within 21 days of learning about the delinquency and file a written request inside 181 days. Get a payoff number before you set the closing date, and have the title company check for judgment liens.

An accepted offer starts the title company's file. It asks the county tax office for a statement, and since Baytown spans two counties you should confirm early which office to call. Payoff letters from each lender are ordered, and the records are searched for judgment liens and unclosed permits.

At the table you sign the deed in front of a notary, and the clerk of the county holding the land records it. Keys normally change hands at funding unless the contract says otherwise. If you are still living in the house, settle a move-out date in writing, along with who covers utilities until then.

sections.h2: Repairs, repair credits and a cash offer
sections.html:
Buyers of older Baytown houses ask about the roof, plumbing and foundation. In a regular listing the inspector notes each problem, and the buyer responds with a repair request or a lower price. A cash buyer inspects once and builds the cost into a single offer, which spares you the back and forth.

Whatever you choose, start by collecting the latest tax statement, any payment plan papers, mortgage payoff figures and permit records for past work, plus the lease if someone rents the house. A complete file helps a buyer decide faster and press for fewer concessions.

faqs.q: Is Baytown in Harris or Chambers County?
faqs.a: Both counties. Baytown is in southeastern Harris County and runs east into western Chambers County. The county on your tax bill decides where the deed is filed and which appraisal district values the lot.

faqs.q: Can I tell a buyer my Baytown house works as a nightly rental?
faqs.a: Not until you have checked with the city. Council has had to approve a Special Use Permit for each one, and an amendment would swap that for a permit process. Planning staff will tell you which rule covers your address.

faqs.q: Is there a time limit to probate a will before I sell?
faqs.a: In general, file the will within four years of the death; a court may still accept it later for good cause. The muniment of title order and the will are then delivered to the clerk of the county where the property is located.

faqs.q: What is a typical home worth in Baytown?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes have a middle value of $197,300 in the 2020-2024 estimates. A given house may fall well on either side of that, depending on its size, age and repairs.

faqs.q: How many people live in Baytown?
faqs.a: Roughly 86,561 as of July 2025, which is 1.2 percent above the 2020 baseline. The city spans 37.00 square miles and had 30,964 households in 2020-2024.
